newsitem.title: USA: Meyer says U.S. core inflation well behaved.
newsitem.headline: Meyer says U.S. core inflation well behaved.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Governor Laurence Meyer said Thursday that the core rate of inflation was behaving very well.
But in remarks to an economics group, Meyer also made clear that there had been some increase in wage rates that bear watching.
He noted that the overall Consumer Price Index had been affected by increases in energy prices but said the core rate, which he called more important, has showed "extraordinary restraint."
He reiterated, however, that the core rate, which excludes food and energy, had certain factors keeping it low but they may be temporary.

"We have to look at the fact that some of the wage numbers are moving upward," he said, adding: "average hourly earnings in particular have moved upward over the last year by a fair amount." He added that broad wage measures have not shown the same increase.
Meyer also said that U.S. exporters have become very competitive in world markets and so he expects exports to do very well in the year ahead.
"It is still one of the solid and strong sectors of the economy," he said.
Asked about the role of the M-2 money measure, Meyer said that while it had become much more stable of late, it still was not ready to assume its previous status.
He also said the upward creep of wages coupled with the difficulty companies have in raising prices could cause some squeeze in corporate profits.
